key_insight: SNAP3D adds physics awareness to single-image part-aware 3D generation so the output is not just visually plausible, but also physically assembleable and stable. It aims to prevent common failure modes like interpenetration, weak connections, and collapse under gravity.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between generating separate 3D parts and producing a valid physical assembly from a single image. Existing methods can create good-looking parts, but they often fail to ensure compatibility, proper contact, and stability when the parts are put together.
method: Use a physics-guided framework to refine single-image part-aware 3D generation.
Enforce physically compatible geometry between neighboring parts to reduce intersections and misalignment.
Promote stable connections so the assembled object can remain structurally valid under gravity.
impact: This is important for practitioners building 3D generation systems for robotics, fabrication, simulation, and interactive editing, where visual quality alone is not enough. Physics-aware part generation can reduce downstream repair work and make generated assets more usable in real-world applications.

paper_title: SNAP3D: Physically Grounded 3D Parts for Assembly from a Single Image
paper_authors: Yu-Rou Tuan, Hao-Tang Tsui, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Kris Kitani, Xiaoxuan Ma
